question.text: At a new-manager onboarding at Himalaya Arbitrage Fund, the compliance head reads out the SEBI definition of 'Hedge Fund' from the AIF Regulations. Which phrase correctly reproduces the SEBI definition given in Section 2.3.3 of the study material?

answer.text: 'An AIF that invests only in listed equity and debt of Indian companies with zero leverage'
'A close-ended fund that invests exclusively in unlisted equity and mezzanine capital of start-ups'
'An AIF which employs diverse or complex trading strategies and invests and trades in securities having diverse risks or complex products including listed and unlisted derivatives'
'An infrastructure-focused AIF that invests in unlisted securities, partnership interests or listed debt of infrastructure SPVs'

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 2.3.3 reproduces SEBI's definition verbatim: a hedge fund is 'an Alternative Investment Fund which employs diverse or complex trading strategies and invests and trades in securities having diverse risks or complex products including listed and unlisted derivatives.' Three features distinguish hedge funds: multi-asset breadth, complex strategies (arbitrage, carry, etc.), and the ability to go long AND short with fund-level leverage. **The Trap:** Option A contradicts the chapter's own notes — hedge funds DO use significant leverage and go both long and short. Option B is the definition of a Venture Capital Fund (Section 2.3.1). Option D is the SEBI definition of an Infrastructure Fund lifted from Section 2.3.4 — a classic cross-category swap trap. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests the same definition for suitability assessment. XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) carries the same text. XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) does NOT — hedge funds sit in Cat III. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Your PPM's 'investment objective' language must map back to this SEBI definition if you want to be classified as a hedge fund under Cat III. If your PPM reads like a long-only listed-equity MF, SEBI can challenge the Cat III classification and pull you toward a mutual-fund structure instead.
